content.text: The text surveys Civil War campaigns from Shiloh through 1863. Confederate forces surprised Grant at Pittsburg Landing, but Buell and Lew Wallace arrived, enabling Union victory; Johnston was killed. McClellan advanced up Virginia’s Peninsula toward Richmond, fought at Seven Pines and Fair Oaks, then Lee’s Seven Days’ Battles forced him to Harrison’s Landing. Jackson’s Valley Campaign diverted Union forces, while Pope lost at Second Bull Run. Lee invaded Maryland but was checked at Antietam, prompting Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation. Union defeat followed at Fredericksburg and Chancellorsville, where Jackson was mortally wounded. Grant captured Vicksburg and Port Hudson, securing the Mississippi. Gettysburg halted Lee’s invasion of Pennsylvania. Subsequent fighting included Chickamauga and the struggle for Chattanooga.
